title: Knowledge check: Representing Relationships in XML

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly covered in “Representing Relationships in XML”?
questions.explanation: The attached XML curriculum lists “Hierarchical relationships” under lesson 31, “Representing Relationships in XML”. The other options are from different topics or unrelated areas.

questions.prompt: Which statement is the most reliable rule to remember when applying “Representing Relationships in XML”?
options: XML describes structured content; it is not a general-purpose programming language.
XML element names are always case-insensitive.
Every XML document must use a DTD.
Whitespace can never be meaningful data.
questions.answer_key: XML describes structured content; it is not a general-purpose programming language.
questions.explanation: XML structures data, but its syntax, encoding, validation, and consuming application must be considered separately.

questions.prompt: After creating an example for “Representing Relationships in XML”, what is the best next step?
options: Verify a normal case, an invalid or boundary case, and document the tool/version used.
Rely on visual appearance without parsing or validation.
Change several parts at once and infer the cause if the result changes.
questions.answer_key: Verify a normal case, an invalid or boundary case, and document the tool/version used.
questions.explanation: A small, reproducible test suite distinguishes expected behavior from a lucky example and makes version assumptions visible.
